questions.context: In a classroom in Tunja, Boyacá, the teacher writes "yesterday" on the board and asks when it happened.

options.text: The day before today.
options.feedback: Correct: yesterday is the past time marker for the previous day.

options.text: The day after today.
options.feedback: Incorrect: the day after today is tomorrow, a future marker.

options.text: Every day of the week.
options.feedback: Incorrect: every day is always, not a past marker.

options.text: A day in the next month.
options.feedback: Incorrect: that is future time, not yesterday.

questions.explanation: Yesterday es un marcador de pasado: señala el día anterior al de hoy y suele acompañar al pasado simple.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: In Pasto, Nariño, a student tells his friend: "I visited my grandmother last week".

options.text: Next week, in the future.
options.feedback: Incorrect: next week points to the future, not the past.

options.text: Every week, always.
options.feedback: Incorrect: that would be every week, a frequency, not past time.

options.text: The week before this week.
options.feedback: Correct: last week locates the action in the past week.

options.text: This week, right now.
options.feedback: Incorrect: this week includes the present, not only the past.

questions.explanation: Last week ubica la acción en la semana pasada. Es otro marcador típico del pasado simple.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: In Neiva, Huila, Sara writes in her diary: "Yesterday I ___ football in the park". She needs the past of "play".

options.text: Yesterday I play football in the park.
options.feedback: Incorrect: play is present; with yesterday we need the past form.

options.text: Yesterday I played football in the park.
options.feedback: Correct: regular verbs add -ed in the past: played.

options.text: Yesterday I playing football in the park.
options.feedback: Incorrect: playing needs was/were, not yesterday alone.

options.text: Yesterday I plays football in the park.
options.feedback: Incorrect: plays is present for he/she, never past.

questions.explanation: Los verbos regulares forman el pasado agregando -ed: play → played. Con yesterday siempre se usa el pasado.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: In Sincelejo, Sucre, two brothers talk: "We ___ at the stadium last week". The verb is "was/were".

options.text: We was at the stadium last week.
options.feedback: Incorrect: was goes with I/he/she, not with we.

options.text: We is at the stadium last week.
options.feedback: Incorrect: is is present; last week needs past.

options.text: We are at the stadium last week.
options.feedback: Incorrect: are is present plural, not past.

options.text: We were at the stadium last week.
options.feedback: Correct: were goes with you/we/they in the past.

questions.explanation: Was se usa con I/he/she/it y were con you/we/they. Como el sujeto es we, lo correcto es were.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: According to the note, what did the writer do last week?
questions.context: Read the note from Valledupar, Cesar: "Hi! Last week I visited Cartagena. I walked on the beach and I watched a beautiful sunset. It was great!"

options.text: Visited Cartagena, walked on the beach and watched a sunset.
options.feedback: Correct: the three past verbs describe exactly what the writer did.

options.text: Stayed at home and played video games.
options.feedback: Incorrect: the note never mentions home or video games.

options.text: Traveled to Bogotá for a concert.
options.feedback: Incorrect: the city in the note is Cartagena, not Bogotá.

options.text: Cooked dinner for his family.
options.feedback: Incorrect: there is no mention of cooking or dinner.

questions.explanation: Comprender un texto en pasado exige identificar los verbos en -ed: visited, walked y watched cuentan lo que hizo el autor.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: In Quibdó, Chocó, a student wrote: "Yesterday I helped my mother, I cleaned my room and I was happy". The teacher asks why all verbs are in the past.

options.text: Because helped, cleaned and was are future forms.
options.feedback: Incorrect: all three are past forms, not future.

options.text: Because yesterday only works with present verbs.
options.feedback: Incorrect: yesterday always requires past verbs.

options.text: Because yesterday sets the whole sentence in the past, so regular verbs take -ed and be becomes was.
options.feedback: Correct: the time marker controls every verb: helped, cleaned (regular) and was (be for I).

options.text: Because the verbs have no relation with yesterday.
options.feedback: Incorrect: yesterday is exactly what forces the past forms.

questions.explanation: Analizar la oración muestra coherencia temporal: yesterday obliga al pasado en todos los verbos, regulares (-ed) e irregulares (was).
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence is correct and why?
questions.context: In Popayán, Cauca, two sentences compete: "She was tired yesterday" and "She were tired yesterday".

options.text: The second, because were goes with she.
options.feedback: Incorrect: were never goes with she; it goes with you/we/they.

options.text: The first, because was goes with she in the past.
options.feedback: Correct: I/he/she/it take was; the subject she requires was.

options.text: Both, because was and were are the same.
options.feedback: Incorrect: they change with the subject and are not interchangeable.

options.text: None, because yesterday cannot go with was.
options.feedback: Incorrect: yesterday combines perfectly with was/were.

questions.explanation: La elección entre was y were depende del sujeto: she es tercera persona singular y exige was.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: How should the report be evaluated and corrected?
questions.context: In Yopal, Casanare, a student presents his weekend report: "Last week I visit my uncle, I play football and I was very happy".

options.text: It is perfect because visit and play are past forms.
options.feedback: Incorrect: visit and play are present; the past forms are visited and played.

options.text: It is perfect because last week works with present verbs.
options.feedback: Incorrect: last week always requires past verbs.

options.text: Only was is wrong and should be is.
options.feedback: Incorrect: was is the only correct verb; is would break the past context.

options.text: It has two errors: visit should be visited and play should be played; only was is correct and must be kept.
options.feedback: Correct: evaluates each verb against last week and fixes exactly the two present forms.

questions.explanation: Evaluar un texto en pasado exige revisar verbo por verbo: los marcadores como last week obligan a formas pasadas (visited, played, was).
questions.subject: ingles
